literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 最终的 MEV 构建体表现出良好的物理化学特性、结构稳定性和令人满意的模型验证。分子对接和动力学模拟显示与 TLR4 的稳定相互作用,而免疫模拟则预测了具有免疫记忆生成的有效体液和细胞 免疫应答。 [10.1038/s41598-026-66934-y]
修正后的表 2 现在准确地呈现了 ITC 测量的参数,解决了各自 RNA 寡聚体和配体数据不一致的问题。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0356274]
母亲接触流感会导致大脑成熟度发生性别和年龄依赖性改变。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10546527/v1]
在 4662 名儿童中,3132 名(67.2%)因 SARS-CoV-2 住院,1530 名(32.8%)因流感住院;婴儿占 SARS-CoV-2 入院人数的三分之一到近一半,而幼儿和学龄儿童则主要是流感入院人数。 [10.1097/inf.0000000000005350]

共有 26,623 名参与者参与其中,其中 4,395 名流感阳性病例和 22,228 名对照者。针对实验室确诊流感的总体 VE 为 46%(95% CI:37-54),跨季节范围为 42% 至 52%。VE 针对乙型流感的效果最高 (64%;95% CI: 49–74),其次是 甲型H3N2流感病毒 (46%;95% CI: 34–56) 和 A(H1N1) (35%;95% CI: 15–51)。 [10.1186/s12879-026-14202-9]

papers.title: Comparison of Epidemiology, Risk Factors, Clinical Presentation and Outcomes of COVID-19 and Seasonal Influenza Among Hospitalized Swiss Children: A Nationwide Prospective Surveillance Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although many children infected with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus type 2 (SARS-CoV-2) or seasonal influenza virus experience a mild course of disease, both infections can lead to hospitalization and, in a subset of children, severe disease requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission for respiratory or cardiac support. To compare the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation and outcomes of children hospitalized with COVID-19 or seasonal influenza, and to identify factors associated with severe disease. METHODS: Data were collected prospectively within a nationwide surveillance system across Swiss hospitals between December 2018 and November 2023. A comparative analysis was performed among children and adolescents (<18 years) hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 or seasonal influenza infection. SARS-CoV-2 data were analyzed according to four time periods defined by the predominantly circulating virus variant: wild type (T1), Alpha (T2), Delta (T3) and Omicron (T4). Influenza data were analyzed across two periods: "pre-COVID" (December 2018 to April 30, 2020) and "during COVID" (May 1, 2020, to November 30, 2023). RESULTS: Of 4662 included children, 3132 (67.2%) were hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 infection and 1530 (32.8%) with influenza. Age distribution differed by virus and period (P < 0.001): infants accounted for one-third to almost half of SARS-CoV-2 admissions (32.2%-46.7%), with adolescents also contributing notably during T1 (22.7%), whereas toddlers and school-aged children were more frequently hospitalized with influenza infection. Fever, cough and rhinitis were the most common symptoms for both viruses. analysis.summary_en: This nationwide prospective surveillance study in Swiss children under 18 years compared hospitalized cases of COVID-19 and seasonal influenza from December 2018 to November 2023. Among 4662 laboratory-confirmed admissions, 67.2% were due to SARS-CoV-2 and 32.8% to influenza. Infants accounted for one-third to nearly half of SARS-CoV-2 admissions, while toddlers and school-aged children were more frequently hospitalized with influenza. Fever, cough and rhinitis were common in both infections, but fever was less frequent during the Omicron wave and the COVID period for influenza. Anosmia occurred only with SARS-CoV-2, whereas acute respiratory distress syndrome and lobar pneumonia (up to 20%) were recorded only among influenza cases. ICU admissions were higher for influenza (10.5–11.8%) than for SARS-CoV-2 (5.0–10.3%), and antibiotic use was greater in influenza (40.7%). Underlying neurological, cardiovascular and respiratory conditions were independently associated with severe disease for both viruses. The authors conclude that influenza in hospitalized children is associated with more severe outcomes than SARS-CoV-2 and recommend broader pediatric influenza vaccination and ongoing surveillance.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2018 年 12 月至 2023 年 11 月,瑞士多家医院进行了一项全国性前瞻性 监测 研究,招募了因实验室确诊的 SARS-CoV-2 或 季节性流感 感染而住院的 18 岁以下儿童和青少年。
elements_zh.methods: SARS-CoV-2病例按四个变体定义的时间段(野生型、Alpha、Delta、Omicron)进行分层,而流感病例则分为新冠肺炎前和新冠肺炎期间;数据是在国家 监测 系统中前瞻性收集的。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 4662 名儿童中,3132 名(67.2%)因 SARS-CoV-2 住院,1530 名(32.8%)因流感住院;婴儿占 SARS-CoV-2 入院人数的三分之一到近一半,而幼儿和学龄儿童则主要是流感入院人数。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在住院儿童中,与 SARS-CoV-2 相比,流感与 ICU 入住率较高(10.5-11.8% vs 5.0-10.3%)、更多并发症(例如,大叶性肺炎高达 20%)、更多抗生素使用(40.7% vs 未明确的较低比率)以及更多呼吸支持相关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持将儿科流感 疫苗接种 扩大到传统高危人群之外,并保持稳健的 监测,以随着病毒变异和模式的演变指导临床和公共卫生决策。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的观察设计和对常规 监测 数据的依赖限制了因果推断和普遍性;由于某些时期可能存在未测量的混杂因素和不完整的症状记录,证据强度被评估为中等。

A comparative analysis was performed among children and adolescents (<18 years) hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 or seasonal influenza infection. SARS-CoV-2 data were analyzed according to four time periods defined by the predominantly circulating virus variant: wild type (T1), Alpha (T2), Delta (T3) and Omicron (T4). Influenza data were analyzed across two periods: "pre-COVID" (December 2018 to April 30, 2020) and "during COVID" (May 1, 2020, to November 30, 2023). RESULTS: Of 4662 included children, 3132 (67.2%) were hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 infection and 1530 (32.8%) with influenza. Age distribution differed by virus and period (P < 0.001): infants accounted for one-third to almost half of SARS-CoV-2 admissions (32.2%-46.7%), with adolescents also contributing notably during T1 (22.7%), whereas toddlers and school-aged children were more frequently hospitalized with influenza infection. Fever, cough and rhinitis were the most common symptoms for both viruses. Among periods with symptom data available, fever was less frequent during SARS-CoV-2 T4 (47.3%) than during earlier SARS-CoV-2 waves (62.8% in T1, 55.7% in T2 and 64.9% in T3) and was also less frequent among children with influenza during the COVID period (26.0%). Anosmia was recorded only among children with SARS-CoV-2 infection (most often during T1: 1.2%; P < 0.001). Proportions of severe symptoms were also similar, except respiratory distress being more common during T4 (12.6%) and with influenza (18.1%; P = 0.02). Acute respiratory distress syndrome was recorded only among children hospitalized with influenza and not among those hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2. ICU admissions were highest during influenza seasons (pre-COVID 10.5% and during COVID 11.8%) compared with 5.0% to 10.3% with SARS-CoV-2 (P = 0.001). Complications were more frequent in children with seasonal influenza (P < 0.001), most commonly lobar pneumonia, which occurred in up to 20% of children with influenza. During T3, deconditioning syndrome was more frequently reported (5.6%) than in other periods. Antibiotic use was higher in children with influenza (40.7% vs. Factors independently associated with severe disease were neurological, cardiovascular and other underlying conditions in children with COVID-19, and neurological and respiratory conditions in children with influenza. CONCLUSIONS: Among hospitalized children with laboratory-confirmed infection, influenza was associated with more frequent ICU admission, complications, antibiotic use and respiratory support than SARS-CoV-2. Although underlying conditions were associated with an increased risk for severe disease, most children had no preexisting underlying conditions. These findings support consideration of broader pediatric influenza vaccination strategies beyond traditional high-risk groups and the need for ongoing surveillance to monitor evolving disease patterns and inform clinical and public health decisions.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:虽然许多感染 2 型严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 (SARS-CoV-2) 或 季节性流感 病毒的儿童病程较轻,但这两种感染都可能导致住院治疗,并且在一部分儿童中,病情严重,需要入住重症监护病房 (ICU) 接受呼吸或心脏支持。比较因 COVID-19 或 季节性流感 住院的儿童的 流行病学、危险因素、临床表现和结果,并确定与严重疾病相关的因素。方法:2018 年 12 月至 2023 年 11 月期间,在瑞士各医院的全国 监测 系统中前瞻性收集数据。对因实验室确诊的 SARS-CoV-2 或 季节性流感 感染而住院的儿童和青少年(<18 岁)进行比较分析。SARS-CoV-2 数据根据主要传播的病毒变体定义的四个时间段进行分析:野生型 (T1)、Alpha (T2)、Delta (T3) 和 Omicron (T4)。流感数据分两个时期进行分析:“新冠疫情前”(2018年12月至2020年4月30日)和“新冠疫情期间”(2020年5月1日至2023年11月30日)。结果:在 4662 名儿童中,3132 名(67.2%)因 SARS-CoV-2 感染住院,1530 名(32.8%)因流感住院。年龄分布因病毒和时期而异(P < 0.001):婴儿占 SARS-CoV-2 入院人数的三分之一到近一半(32.2%-46.7%),青少年在 T1 期间的贡献也显着(22.7%),而幼儿和学龄儿童因流感感染住院的情况更为常见。发烧、咳嗽和鼻炎是这两种病毒最常见的症状。在有症状数据的时期中,SARS-CoV-2 T4 期间的发烧频率 (47.3%) 低于早期 SARS-CoV-2 波期间的发烧频率(T1 中为 62.8%,T2 中为 55.7%,T3 中为 64.9%),并且在 COVID 期间感染流感的儿童中发烧频率也较低(26.0%)。仅在感染 SARS-CoV-2 的儿童中记录到嗅觉丧失(最常见于 T1:1.2%;P < 0.001)。严重症状的比例也相似,但呼​​吸窘迫在 T4 期间(12.6%)和流感期间(18.1%;P = 0.02)更常见。仅在因流感住院的儿童中记录了急性呼吸窘迫综合征,而在因 SARS-CoV-2 住院的儿童中未记录到。流感季节期间 ICU 入院率最高(新冠肺炎前为 10.5%,新冠肺炎期间为 11.8%),而 SARS-CoV-2 则为 5.0% 至 10.3%(P = 0.001)。季节性流感 儿童的并发症更为常见 (P < 0.001),最常见的是大叶性肺炎,高达 20% 的流感儿童发生这种情况。在 T3 期间,与其他时期相比,失调综合征的报告频率更高(5.6%)。流感儿童的抗生素使用率较高(40.7%,而与严重疾病独立相关的因素是 COVID-19 儿童的神经系统、心血管和其他基础疾病,以及流感儿童的神经系统和呼吸系统疾病。结论:在实验室确诊感染的住院儿童中,与 SARS-CoV-2 相比,流感与更频繁的 ICU 入住、并发症、抗生素使用和呼吸支持相关。尽管基础疾病与严重疾病风险增加相关,但大多数儿童没有预先存在的基础疾病这些发现支持考虑超越传统高危人群的更广泛的儿科流感 疫苗接种 策略,以及持续使用 监测 来监测不断变化的疾病模式并为临床和公共卫生决策提供信息的必要性。

analysis_zh.main_results: 在 4662 名儿童中,3132 名(67.2%)因 SARS-CoV-2 住院,1530 名(32.8%)因流感住院;婴儿占 SARS-CoV-2 入院人数的三分之一到近一半,而幼儿和学龄儿童则主要是流感入院人数。

papers.title: Deciphering influenza B virus-derived peptides and their presentation by HLA class I molecules.
papers.abstract: Despite influenza vaccines being widely available, influenza still causes significant morbidity and mortality annually. Vaccines typically induce humoral-mediated protection against rapidly mutating surface glycoproteins, necessitating that they be updated and administered each year. In contrast, CD8+ T cells, which can control and clear viral infections, can recognise more conserved viral epitopes. Therefore, there is considerable interest in understanding CD8+ T cell responses to influenza virus for the development of future vaccines and therapeutics. Although Alphainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUAV) and Betainfluenzavirus influenzae (FLUBV) co-circulate in humans and both contribute to seasonal epidemics, there is limited data regarding CD8+ T cell responses to FLUBV. This knowledge gap spans both immunological and molecular insights. In the present review, we summarise the current knowledge of FLUBV-derived CD8+ T cell epitopes at both cellular and molecular levels, in comparison with FLUAV. Collectively, this highlights the limited data available on FLUBV, despite its significant role in human influenza infections.

papers.title: Development of a multi-species luciferase-based double-antigen ELISA for the detection of antibodies against influenza A virus H5 clade 2.3.4.4b
papers.abstract: The highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses of subtype H5N1 represent a major threat to animal and public health. The current panzootic with H5 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused numerous, widespread outbreaks in various domestic and wild avian species with high mortalities, massive losses, and a high frequency of spillover events to unexpected novel mammalian hosts, such as dairy cows. The global H5N1 situation raises serious concerns about zoonotic risks due to effective mammal-to-mammal transmission. Therefore, it is critical to increase surveillance intensity of a broadened species range, particularly at the human-animal interface. For this purpose, reliable and cost-effective serological tools that are easy to perform and suitable for high-throughput screening are critically needed. The newly developed double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay format employing a luminescence-based detection technology has demonstrated compliance with such prerequisites. The assay allowed sensitive and specific detection of antibodies directed against H5 hemagglutinin of clade 2.3.4.4b in a wide range of birds and mammals, including humans. Furthermore, it allowed differentiating H5 anti-head-specific from cross-reacting anti-stalk antibodies, which represents a valuable feature with regard to the monitoring of future vaccination programs with H5-specific vaccines. Thus, the assay is a significant contribution to existing serological diagnostic tests for a clade-optimized and species-independent detection of influenza A virus antibodies. IMPORTANCE: The ongoing highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 panzootic has caused numerous outbreaks in domestic and wild animals, with frequent spillover events to unexpected host species, which underscores the importance of intensified surveillance. However, sensitive and specific multi-species serological assays represent a major gap. For this purpose, we developed a novel double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay that employs an innovative luminescence-based readout strategy. The test allowed a highly sensitive and specific detection of H5-specific antibodies in a wide range of avian and mammalian species, including humans. It therefore represents a valuable contribution to improving species-independent serological diagnostic tools for the detection of influenza A virus antibodies.

source_records.abstract: The highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses of subtype H5N1 represent a major threat to animal and public health. The current panzootic with H5 clade 2.3.4.4b has caused numerous, widespread outbreaks in various domestic and wild avian species with high mortalities, massive losses, and a high frequency of spillover events to unexpected novel mammalian hosts, such as dairy cows. The global H5N1 situation raises serious concerns about zoonotic risks due to effective mammal-to-mammal transmission. Therefore, it is critical to increase surveillance intensity of a broadened species range, particularly at the human-animal interface. For this purpose, reliable and cost-effective serological tools that are easy to perform and suitable for high-throughput screening are critically needed. The newly developed double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay format employing a luminescence-based detection technology has demonstrated compliance with such prerequisites. The assay allowed sensitive and specific detection of antibodies directed against H5 hemagglutinin of clade 2.3.4.4b in a wide range of birds and mammals, including humans. Furthermore, it allowed differentiating H5 anti-head-specific from cross-reacting anti-stalk antibodies, which represents a valuable feature with regard to the monitoring of future vaccination programs with H5-specific vaccines. Thus, the assay is a significant contribution to existing serological diagnostic tests for a clade-optimized and species-independent detection of influenza A virus antibodies. IMPORTANCE: The ongoing highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 panzootic has caused numerous outbreaks in domestic and wild animals, with frequent spillover events to unexpected host species, which underscores the importance of intensified surveillance. However, sensitive and specific multi-species serological assays represent a major gap. For this purpose, we developed a novel double-antigen enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay that employs an innovative luminescence-based readout strategy. The test allowed a highly sensitive and specific detection of H5-specific antibodies in a wide range of avian and mammalian species, including humans. It therefore represents a valuable contribution to improving species-independent serological diagnostic tools for the detection of influenza A virus antibodies.

papers.title: Seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness in Thailand, 2022–2025: a multi-season test-negative design study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Seasonal influenza vaccination is a key public health strategy for reducing influenza-related morbidity and mortality. In Thailand, influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) is routinely evaluated using surveillance data; however, VE may vary by season, virus subtype, and population subgroup. Continuous monitoring is essential to inform vaccination policy and program performance. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study using a test-negative design to estimate influenza VE in Thailand from 2022 to 2025. Data were obtained from sentinel surveillance across nine hospitals in four regions, including Bangkok. Patients presenting with influenza-like illness (ILI) or severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) who were tested for influenza by RT-PCR were included. Cases were influenza-positive patients, and controls were influenza-negative patients. Vaccination status was based on self-report and verified through medical records or registry data, with vaccination defined as receipt of influenza vaccine at least 14 days prior to symptom onset. VE was estimated using mixed-effects logistic regression adjusted for age group, sex, comorbidity, obesity, patient severity, epidemiologic week, and influenza season, with hospital included as a random effect. Results A total of 26,623 participants were included, comprising 4,395 influenza-positive cases and 22,228 controls. Overall VE against laboratory-confirmed influenza was 46% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 37–54). VE was relatively consistent across seasons (42% to 52%). By subtype, VE was highest against influenza B (64%; 95% CI: 49–74), followed by A(H3N2) (46%; 95% CI: 34–56) and A(H1N1) (35%; 95% CI: 15–51). Subgroup analyses showed higher VE among adults aged 18–64 years (57%; 95% CI: 44–67) and lower, non-significant VE among young children and older adults. VE was higher among outpatients than among severe cases. Conclusions Seasonal influenza vaccination provided moderate protection against laboratory-confirmed influenza in Thailand, with consistent effectiveness across multiple seasons. These findings support continued influenza vaccination programs and highlight the importance of ongoing VE monitoring to inform public health policy and improve vaccination strategies, particularly among high-risk populations.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 季节性流感 疫苗接种 是减少流感相关发病率和 死亡率 的关键公共卫生策略。在泰国,流感 疫苗 有效性(VE)通常使用 监测 数据进行评估;然而,VE 可能因季节、病毒亚型和人群亚组而异。持续监控对于告知 疫苗接种 政策和计划绩效至关重要。方法 我们使用测试阴性设计进行了一项回顾性观察研究,以估计 2022 年至 2025 年泰国的流感 VE。数据从包括曼谷在内的四个地区的 9 家医院的哨点 监测 获得。包括患有流感样疾病 (ILI) 或严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 并通过 RT-PCR 进行流感检测的患者。病例是流感阳性患者,对照是流感阴性患者。疫苗接种 状态基于自我报告,并通过医疗记录或登记数据进行验证,疫苗接种 定义为在症状出现前至少 14 天感染 疫苗 流感。使用混合效应逻辑回归估计 VE,并根据年龄组、性别、合并症、肥胖、患者严重程度、流行病学周和流感季节进行调整,并将医院作为随机效应纳入其中。结果 总共纳入 26,623 名参与者,其中 4,395 名流感阳性病例和 22,228 名对照者。针对实验室确诊流感的总体 VE 为 46%(95% 置信区间 [CI]:37-54)。不同季节的 VE 相对一致(42% 至 52%)。按亚型划分,VE 对抗乙型流感最高 (64%;95% CI: 49–74),其次是 甲型H3N2流感病毒 (46%;95% CI: 34–56) 和 A(H1N1) (35%;95% CI: 15–51)。亚组分析显示,18-64 岁成年人的 VE 较高(57%;95% CI:44-67),而幼儿和老年人的 VE 较低,但不显着。门诊患者的 VE 高于重症病例。结论 季节性流感 疫苗接种 对泰国实验室确诊的流感提供了中等程度的保护,且在多个季节均具有一致的有效性。这些发现支持持续的流感 疫苗接种 计划,并强调持续 VE 监测对于为公共卫生政策提供信息和改进 疫苗接种 策略的重要性,特别是在高危人群中。

papers.title: Pre-existing and breadth of immunity to seasonal influenza viruses among community-dwelling older adults in Thailand
papers.abstract: Older adults are at high risk for influenza-associated morbidity and mortality. Monitoring influenza immunity in this population is crucial for disease prevention and control. However, data on immunity to seasonal influenza viruses among elderly populations remain limited. This study aimed to characterize the quantity, functional quality, and breadth of antibody responses to circulating influenza viruses among community-dwelling elderly in Thailand. A total of 442 plasma samples from elderly individuals aged ≥ 60 years residing in high-density urban communities in central Thailand, collected during 2022–2023, were analyzed. Antibody responses to four representative circulating A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and type B (Victoria and Yamagata lineages) influenza viruses were assessed using hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) and microneutralization (MNT) assays. In accordance with World Health Organization guidance on influenza vaccination, seroprotection is defined as HAI titers equal to or exceeding 40. Most elderly individuals exhibited pre-existing antibodies to all circulating influenza viruses. HAI titers and seroprotection rates were higher against influenza B viruses than influenza A viruses, with the weakest responses observed against A/H3N2. In contrast, neutralizing (NT) antibodies were universally detectable, with NT titers consistently exceeding HAI titers across all strains. Despite exhibiting the highest HAI titers against B/Victoria lineage, this virus showed the highest HAI to MNT ratio, indicating reduced functional antibody quality. Older age (≥ 65 years) and female were associated with higher HAI titers against influenza A viruses; however, these factors did not consistently translate into increased NT activity. Only 15.6% of the older adults exhibited broad antibodies against all four circulating strains, indicating limited cross-strain breadth. papers.abstract_zh: 老年人患流感相关发病和 死亡率 的风险很高。监测该人群的流感免疫力对于疾病预防和控制至关重要。然而,老年人群对 季节性流感 病毒免疫力的数据仍然有限。本研究旨在表征泰国社区老年人对流行流感病毒的抗体反应的数量、功能质量和广度。对 2022 年至 2023 年间居住在泰国中部高密度城市社区的 60 岁以上老年人的总共 442 份血浆样本进行了分析。使用血凝抑制 (HAI) 和微量中和 (MNT) 测定评估对四种代表性循环 A/H1N1、A/H3N2 和 B 型(维多利亚和山形谱系)流感病毒的抗体反应。根据世界卫生组织关于流感的指南 疫苗接种,血清保护被定义为 HAI 滴度等于或超过 40。大多数老年人表现出针对所有流行流感病毒的预先存在的抗体。针对乙型流感病毒的 HAI 滴度和血清保护率高于甲型流感病毒,针对 A/H3N2 的反应最弱。相比之下,中和 (NT) 抗体普遍可检测到,所有菌株的 NT 滴度始终超过 HAI 滴度。尽管针对 B/Victoria 谱系表现出最高的 HAI 滴度,但该病毒表现出最高的 HAI 与 MNT 比率,表明功能性抗体质量降低。年龄较大(≥ 65 岁)和女性与针对甲型流感病毒的 HAI 滴度较高相关;然而,这些因素并没有始终如一地转化为 NT 活性的增加。只有 15.6% 的老年人表现出针对所有四种流行菌株的广泛抗体,表明交叉菌株广度有限。老年人群对季节性流感 A和B病毒表现出预先存在的免疫力;然而,这些观察到的血清学结果是异质的,具有很强的毒株特异性,并且广度有限,与 A/H3N2 存在显着差距。MNT 评估的功能免疫可能与基于 HAI 的估计不同,这强调结合抗体功能质量评估可以为流感 监测 提供补充信息。这些数据提供了全面的血清监测,并支持使用增强的 疫苗接种 策略来减轻老龄化人群中流感相关的风险。

papers.title: Sex-specific trajectories of adolescent brain maturation and sensorimotor gating after maternal influenza infection in mice
papers.abstract: Maternal infection during pregnancy is increasingly recognised as a risk factor for neurodevelopmental disorders, yet how a clinically relevant viral insult reshapes brain maturation remains poorly defined. Here, we used a live influenza A virus model of maternal immune activation (MIA) to examine whether prenatal infection alters offspring brain development across adolescence. Pregnant mice were infected at embryonic day 12, and offspring underwent longitudinal high-field MRI at 5, 8, 11 and 14 weeks, followed by prepulse inhibition (PPI) testing as a measure of sensorimotor gating. Maternal influenza exposure produced sex- and age-dependent alterations in brain maturation. Atlas-based volumetry identified FDR-corrected sex- and age-dependent treatment-related effects in the hippocampal CA1 region, while tensor-based morphometry revealed dynamic structural changes across sensory cortices, insula, hippocampus and thalamus. Network analyses further showed disrupted inter-regional structural coordination, particularly in males during early–mid adolescence. Despite partial normalisation of network architecture by late adolescence, influenza-exposed offspring displayed impaired PPI. Partial least squares regression linked these behavioural deficits to altered developmental trajectories in somatosensory cortex, medulla and pons. These findings show that maternal influenza infection does not simply produce static brain abnormalities but alters the trajectory and coordination of adolescent brain maturation in a sex-, region- and circuit-specific manner with long-term behavioural consequences. This work identifies developmental windows and neural systems that may guide future strategies to prevent or reverse infection-associated neurodevelopmental vulnerability.

Introduction Neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), likely arise from altered developmental trajectories beginning prenatally, when the foetal brain is sensitive to genetic, immune and environmental cues1,2. Although these disorders are highly heritable3, genetics alone cannot account for their onset, timing or clinical heterogeneity4. The prenatal period represents a critical window, when factors like maternal infection and inflammation may act to shape later neuropsychiatric trajectories and outcomes5–7, including influenza virus-related immune activation increasing the risk for schizophrenia-related outcomes8. However, the biological events linking a transient maternal immune challenge to long-term changes in offspring brain maturation remain difficult to resolve in humans. Preclinical models therefore provide an essential platform to identify vulnerable developmental windows, circuits and behaviours that are most vulnerable to disruption from early insults, without the ethical concern as in human study9,10. Maternal immune activation (MIA) provides a powerful experimental framework to model how infection or inflammation during pregnancy alters offspring brain development11. Traditionally, MIA has been induced using immune mimetics such as polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid [poly(I:C)], lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-612,13. These approaches establish that maternal immune responses can disrupt neurodevelopment without direct foetal infection12,13. However, immune mimetics capture only part of the biology of maternal infection. In contrast, live influenza A virus (IAV) engages viral sensing pathways, antiviral immunity, cytokine induction, antibody responses and systemic maternal pathology, including inflammatory and vascular dysfunction14,15. This distinction is critical, because clinically relevant maternal viral infection is not a single immune signal, but a coordinated and dynamic host response. Live-virus MIA models may therefore better represent how maternal infection reshapes foetal and postnatal brain development15. Longitudinal neuroimaging can reveal how prenatal immune challenge alters trajectories of brain maturation16,17, where MIA effects may emerge, evolve or partially normalise across adolescence16. Structural MRI enables repeated, non-invasive assessment of regional brain growth, and tensor-based morphometry (TBM) can quantify both anatomically defined and spatially localised brain changes. The hippocampus is of particular interest because of its role in learning, memory and spatial navigation, has well-established involvement in schizophrenia and related disorders18–21, and is implicated in MIA-associated brain pathology22,23. Longitudinal analysis of its subfields may therefore identify specific time-variant disruptions rather than a whole-region measure. To understand the mechanistic bridge between prenatal immune challenge and later-emerging abnormalities, prepulse inhibition (PPI) provides a behavioural readout of sensorimotor gating, which is disrupted in schizophrenia and other neurodevelopmental disorders24. PPI deficits occur in both human cohorts with schizophrenia and pre-clinical MIA models, including our previous work showing impaired PPI in IAV-infected dams24–26. However, most studies have treated PPI and other behaviours as endpoint phenotypes, with limited insight into the developmental brain trajectories that give rise to impairment. Linking longitudinal MRI to PPI can identify the regions and maturational patterns associated with impaired sensorimotor gating after prenatal viral immune challenge. Here, we leveraged a clinically relevant live IAV model of MIA to determine how prenatal viral immune challenge alters offspring brain maturation across adolescence. Pregnant mice were infected at embryonic day 12, and offspring underwent longitudinal high-field MRI at 5, 8, 11 and 14 weeks, followed by PPI testing in early adulthood. We combined atlas-based segmentation, longitudinal tensor-based morphometry, inter-regional structural correlation network analysis and partial least squares (PLS) regression to define how maternal IAV exposure affects regional brain growth, local morphometry, network organisation and structure–behaviour relationships. We focused particularly on sex-specific effects, given the known sex bias in neurodevelopmental vulnerability following prenatal immune challenge. This design allows us to move beyond static endpoint measures to test whether maternal influenza disrupts the tempo of adolescent brain maturation, creating circuit-level vulnerabilities that persist as impaired sensorimotor gating. Materials and Methods Animals and maternal influenza infection All animal experiments were conducted at the Baker Institute Animal Facility (PAC) and Imaging Facility in Melbourne, Australia, in accordance with the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) of Australia guidelines for animal experimentation and with approval from Animal Ethics Committee of the Monash Institute of Pharmaceutical Sciences (AEC# 29379). C57BL/6J breeding mice were obtained from the Monash Animal Research Platform and acclimatised for 7 days before time-mating. Females were paired with males at a 1:1 ratio. Mice were housed under a 12 h light/dark cycle at 22°C and 40–60% humidity, with standard chow and water available ad libitum. Plugged dams were housed individually in micro-isolator cages. Mouse-adapted HKx31 influenza A virus (IAV; H3N2) was propagated in 10-day- old embryonated chicken eggs. Viral titres were quantified by plaque assay using Madin-Darby Canine Kidney cells, as previously described27, and virus stocks were stored at −80°C. At embryonic day 12 (E12) of pregnancy, dams were anesthetised with isoflurane and randomly allocated to either the IAV group or phosphate buffered saline (PBS) control group in a balanced 1:1 design (n = 4 dams per group). Dams received intranasal inoculation with either 35μl of 103 PFU IAV or PBS as previously described27. This dose and gestational timing were selected because they induce MIA while minimising offspring lethality15. Maternal body weight was recorded daily from E12 to E16, after which dams were left undisturbed until delivery at approximately E19–E20. Offspring were weaned at 3–3.5 weeks of age and group-housed by sex, with 2–5 mice per cage, under reverse light-cycle conditions. Following completion of behavioural testing, mice were rested for 2–3 days and then euthanised by cervical dislocation. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) acquisition Longitudinal in vivo MRI was performed at 5 (early adolescence), 8 (mid adolescence), 11 (late adolescence) and 14 (early adulthood) weeks of age using a 9.4T small-animal MRI scanner with a mouse room-temperature surface coil (Bruker, USA). Immediately before scanning, mice were anaesthetised using 5% isoflurane in 0.5 – 1L/min in medical grade oxygen and positioned in an MRI compatible animal holder with anaesthesia maintained via a nose cone. Isoflurane concentration was adjusted throughout scanning to maintain stable anaesthesia. Respiratory rate was monitored via a pressure sensor and maintained within 45 – 70 breaths per minute. Body temperature was monitored using a rectal probe and maintained at 37°C with a purpose-built circulating hot-water warming system. Multi-echo gradient echo (GRE) scans were acquired with the following parameters: echo time (TE) 2.1 ms; inter-echo spacing (dTE) 3.1 ms, 12 echoes; Repetition Time (TR) 66 ms; matrix size 174x144x80; Field of View (FOV) 17.4x14.4x8 mm^3; voxel size 100 x 100 x 100 μm3; and four repetitions. *Figure 1 here* Atlas-based volumetric analysis Multi-echo T2*-weighted images were corrected for bias-field inhomogeneity using N4ITK and averaged across echoes to improve anatomical contrast28. Brain extraction was performed using Brain Extraction Net, which was first fine-tuned using existing skull-stripped mouse MRI data and then applied to the full dataset29. The ANTs software toolkit28 was used for volumetric analysis to create group-specific templates for each treatment and sex at each time point, which were then merged to form a comprehensive study template. This study template underwent nonlinear registration to the Allen Mouse Brain CCFv3 using AIDAmri based on NiftyReg, enabling us to accurately segment brain areas (including hippocampal subfields)28,30,31. Nonlinear registrations were applied from individual subject images to the study template for precise region of interest delineation. Manual adjustments were made where necessary on the study template mask. Finally, each region volume was determined by counting the number of voxels it contained. A linear mixed-effects model was employed in MATLAB using the ‘fitlme’ function to investigate the interaction of treatment group, sex, and age on brain region volumes longitudinally. Random effects included intercepts for individual animals and fixed effects for treatment, sex, and age, with age modelled using linear, quadratic and cubic terms. Model residuals were tested for normality using a Q-Q plot and histogram overlaying a standard normal distribution, in addition to using the Lilliefors test for normality corroboration. This model accounted for the fixed effects of treatment group, sex, and age, as well as their interactions up to the cubic term for age, thereby effectively handling longitudinal repeated measures data. P-values from the atlas-based volumetric analysis were corrected for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Tensor-Based Morphometry (TBM) Tensor-based morphometry was used to assess localised differences in brain morphology across development. Aligned raw data from each individual were initially registered to a Minimum Deformation Template (MDT) created from PBS images. Non-linear registrations of individuals to MDT were performed to obtain the absolute Jacobian determinants, ensuring local anatomical variations were captured and facilitating exact comparison of morphological differences across individuals. Following registration, deformation fields from each individual data to the MDT were analysed by the log Jacobian determinant, providing a voxel-wise representation of local volume changes rate (expansion or contraction) relative to the MDT. Statistical analysis of TBM data was completed using linear mixed effects model — voxel-wise models were used to examine treatment group, sex, and age effects while accounting for longitudinal data structure. Fixed effects included treatment group, sex, and age, together with their interactions. Random effects included individual intercepts. A permutation (5000 times random shuffling of treatment and sex labels) approach for correction in multiple comparisons was used for data analysis. At each permutation, clusters of voxels with statistical significance greater than |t| > 3 were identified, and the maximum sum of the t-statistic over voxels in each cluster was taken. Significant threshold p-values were thus identified using the resulting distribution of maximum sums under the null. Graph theoretical analysis of inter-regional structural correlations Graph theoretical analyses were used to examine whether maternal IAV exposure altered the coordination of regional brain growth across development. For each sex and treatment group, Spearman’s rank correlation matrices were generated from longitudinal changes in regional brain volumes. Correlations were calculated between all pairs of brain regions using percentage volume change across consecutive imaging intervals: 5–8 weeks, 8–11 weeks, and 11– 14 weeks. This approach allowed us to assess whether regional brain maturation occurred in a coordinated or disrupted manner across development. Correlation matrices were thresholded at Spearman’s ρ = 0.625 to retain robust inter-regional associations while reducing the influence of weak or potentially spurious correlations. Network organisation was then assessed using graph theoretical metrics, including Jaccard similarity index, characteristic path length, assortativity, closeness centrality and transitivity. Jaccard similarity was used to quantify the similarity of network architecture between treatment groups, characteristic path length to assess global network integration, assortativity to determine whether nodes preferentially connected with other nodes of similar degree, closeness centrality to estimate nodal communication efficiency, and transitivity to assess local clustering. Community structure was examined using the Louvain method. Prepulse inhibition (PPI) testing Prepulse inhibition test was conducted 3-4 days after the final MRI scan at 14 weeks of age. Mice underwent a mock PPI session for habituation, followed by the test session 24 h later, as described previously15,25. Two-way ANOVA was conducted to examine main effects of treatment (PBS vs. IAV) and sex, and their interactions, followed by post hoc analyses where appropriate. Structure–behaviour modelling Partial least squares (PLS) regression was used to explore correlations between structural brain developmental trajectory parameters (intercept, 1st, 2nd, 3rd order coefficients) and behavioural performance in the PPI test. However, immune mimetics capture only part of the biology of maternal infection. In contrast, live influenza A virus (IAV) engages viral sensing pathways, antiviral immunity, cytokine induction, antibody responses and systemic maternal pathology, including inflammatory and vascular dysfunction14,15. This distinction is critical, because clinically relevant maternal viral infection is not a single immune signal, but a coordinated and dynamic host response. Live-virus MIA models may therefore better represent how maternal infection reshapes foetal and postnatal brain development15. Longitudinal neuroimaging can reveal how prenatal immune challenge alters trajectories of brain maturation16,17, where MIA effects may emerge, evolve or partially normalise across adolescence16. Structural MRI enables repeated, non-invasive assessment of regional brain growth, and tensor-based morphometry (TBM) can quantify both anatomically defined and spatially localised brain changes. The hippocampus is of particular interest because of its role in learning, memory and spatial navigation, has well-established involvement in schizophrenia and related disorders18–21, and is implicated in MIA-associated brain pathology22,23. Longitudinal analysis of its subfields may therefore identify specific time-variant disruptions rather than a whole-region measure. To understand the mechanistic bridge between prenatal immune challenge and later-emerging abnormalities, prepulse inhibition (PPI) provides a behavioural readout of sensorimotor gating, which is disrupted in schizophrenia and other neurodevelopmental disorders24. PPI deficits occur in both human cohorts with schizophrenia and pre-clinical MIA models, including our previous work showing impaired PPI in IAV-infected dams24–26. papers.abstract_original: Maternal infection during pregnancy is increasingly recognised as a risk factor for neurodevelopmental disorders, yet how a clinically relevant viral insult reshapes brain maturation remains poorly defined. Here, we used a live influenza A virus model of maternal immune activation (MIA) to examine whether prenatal infection alters offspring brain development across adolescence. Pregnant mice were infected at embryonic day 12, and offspring underwent longitudinal high-field MRI at 5, 8, 11 and 14 weeks, followed by prepulse inhibition (PPI) testing as a measure of sensorimotor gating. Maternal influenza exposure produced sex- and age-dependent alterations in brain maturation. Atlas-based volumetry identified FDR-corrected sex- and age-dependent treatment-related effects in the hippocampal CA1 region, while tensor-based morphometry revealed dynamic structural changes across sensory cortices, insula, hippocampus and thalamus. Network analyses further showed disrupted inter-regional structural coordination, particularly in males during early–mid adolescence. Despite partial normalisation of network architecture by late adolescence, influenza-exposed offspring displayed impaired PPI. Partial least squares regression linked these behavioural deficits to altered developmental trajectories in somatosensory cortex, medulla and pons. These findings show that maternal influenza infection does not simply produce static brain abnormalities but alters the trajectory and coordination of adolescent brain maturation in a sex-, region- and circuit-specific manner with long-term behavioural consequences. This work identifies developmental windows and neural systems that may guide future strategies to prevent or reverse infection-associated neurodevelopmental vulnerability.

papers.title: Emergence of an antigenically drifted and reassorted influenza B virus at the end of the 2024–25 influenza season
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Influenza B virus (IBV) is a significant contributor to annual and severe cases of influenza, particularly in the young and elderly. Late in the 2024–25 Northern Hemisphere influenza season, a surge of IBV cases was identified in the Johns Hopkins Hospital Systems. The IBV responsible for the surge, C.3.1/re, was a clade C.3 virus that had reassorted with clade C.5.1 viruses and acquired the D197N mutation in hemagglutinin, restoring a putative N-linked glycan predicted to mask a key neutralizing antibody epitope. The C.3.1/re viruses preferentially infected children but showed no significant change in disease severity. C.3.1/re viruses were poorly neutralized by pre- and post-influenza vaccination serum in a human cohort. The removal of the glycan at residue 197 restored neutralizing antibody recognition. The C.3.1/re IBV genotype that emerged late in the 2024–25 influenza season was antigenically mismatched with IBV vaccine strains for the 2025 and 2026 Southern hemisphere, as well as the 2025–26 Northern Hemisphere influenza seasons. While the 2026–27 Northern Hemisphere vaccine strain is a C.3.1/re, the egg-adapted isolate selected (B/Tokyo/EIS13-175/2025) lacks the 197 glycosylation which is predicted to have poor recognition with circulating IBV clades. Phylogenetic analysis of currently circulating IBVs shows a diversification of circulating C.3 clades with multiple reassortment events between C.3 and C.5 clades in addition to independent acquisitions of D197N mutations, suggesting IBV is going through a period of significant antigenic and genetic expansion. IMPORTANCE Influenza B viruses are undergoing a period of antigenic and genetic expansion, with several reassorted viruses emerging that also contain point mutations in key hemagglutinin antigenic sites proximal to the receptor binding domain. This has important impacts on vaccine strain choice, as only one IBV component is included in current influenza vaccines. We demonstrate a significant shift in the demographics of IBV-infected individuals with the emergence of the antigenically drifted and reassorted IBV C.3.1/re. Furthermore, we show that 197 glycosylation of hemagglutinin is critical for C.3.1/re antigenic drift, and we document several emergent C.3 reassortments encoding the D197N mutation. With the IBV vaccine component for the Northern Hemisphere 2026–27 season having lost a key N-linked glycan on the hemagglutinin protein, and multiple independent emergences of antigenically drifted and reassorted viruses, attention to IBV infections should be increased in the upcoming Southern and Northern hemisphere influenza seasons.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza B virus (IBV) contributes substantially to annual influenza burden, particularly in children and the elderly, yet its antigenic and genetic evolution challenges vaccine strain selection and effectiveness. The study addresses a knowledge gap regarding the emergence of antigenically drifted and reassorted IBV variants late in the 2024–25 season and their implications for vaccine mismatch.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated a surge of IBV cases in the Johns Hopkins Hospital Systems late in the 2024–25 Northern Hemisphere influenza season. It characterized the antigenically drifted and reassorted IBV C.3.1/re genotype and assessed its antigenic properties using human serum cohorts and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis.methods: Phylogenetic analysis was performed to trace the emergence and reassortment events of C.3.1/re viruses. Neutralizing antibody responses were measured in human cohorts using pre- and post-vaccination serum against C.3.1/re viruses. The role of hemagglutinin glycosylation at residue 197 was evaluated by removing the glycan and testing neutralization.
analysis.main_results: The C.3.1/re viruses preferentially infected children and showed no significant change in disease severity compared to other IBV infections. C.3.1/re viruses were poorly neutralized by pre- and post-influenza vaccination serum in a human cohort. Removal of the glycan at residue 197 restored neutralizing antibody recognition.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The emergence of C.3.1/re IBV with the D197N mutation and reassortment events indicates a period of significant antigenic and genetic expansion in IBV. analysis.summary_en: This study describes the emergence of an antigenically drifted and reassorted influenza B virus (IBV) genotype, C.3.1/re, late in the 2024–25 Northern Hemisphere influenza season, identified in the Johns Hopkins Hospital Systems. The C.3.1/re viruses preferentially infected children and exhibited poor neutralization by pre- and post-vaccination human serum, indicating antigenic mismatch with vaccine strains. Phylogenetic analysis revealed multiple reassortment events between C.3 and C.5 clades and independent acquisitions of the D197N mutation, which restores a glycan masking a key neutralizing epitope. Removal of the glycan at residue 197 restored antibody recognition, demonstrating its critical role in antigenic drift. These findings underscore the need for enhanced surveillance and adaptive vaccine strain selection to address the expanding antigenic diversity of IBV.

papers.full_text: Abstract Influenza A(H3N2) continues to pose a significant global public health challenge owing to its rapid antigenic evolution, particularly within the hemagglutinin (HA) glycoprotein, which frequently compromises vaccine effectiveness. The emergence of the H3N2 subclade K (J.2.4.1), characterized by multiple antigenically relevant mutations, necessitates the development of updated vaccine strategies capable of eliciting strain-specific immune responses. In this study, an immunoinformatics driven approach was employed to design a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) targeting the HA protein of the J.2.4.1 variant. The HA sequence was modified to incorporate lineage-specific mutations, and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were predicted using the machine learning-based NetMHCpan/NetMHCIIpan algorithms and the IEDB platform. High-confidence epitopes were selected based on antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and immunogenic potential, and assembled using appropriate linkers with the 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as an adjuvant. The final MEV construct demonstrated favorable physicochemical characteristics, structural stability, and satisfactory model validation. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations revealed stable interactions between the vaccine construct and TLR4, while immune simulation predicted effective humoral and cellular immune responses with the generation of immunological memory. Population coverage analysis further indicated broad global applicability of the selected T-cell epitopes. Together, these findings suggest that the incorporation of J.2.4.1 specific antigenic mutations into the MEV may enhance strain-specific immune recognition and provide a promising computational framework for the rapid development of next-generation influenza vaccines. Nevertheless, experimental validation is required to confirm the immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy of the proposed vaccine candidate. analysis.study_design_and_population: This study employed an immunoinformatics-driven approach to design a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) targeting the HA protein of the H3N2 subclade K (J.2.4.1) variant. analysis.methods: The HA sequence was modified to include lineage-specific mutations, and cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were predicted using NetMHCpan/NetMHCIIpan algorithms and the IEDB platform. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as suggesting that incorporating J.2.4.1-specific antigenic mutations into the MEV may enhance strain-specific immune recognition, providing a promising computational framework for rapid next-generation influenza vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study offers a computational strategy for designing strain-specific influenza vaccines targeting emerging variants, potentially informing future surveillance and vaccine strain selection to improve vaccine effectiveness against H3N2 subclade K.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the public health challenge posed by the rapid antigenic evolution of influenza A(H3N2), particularly the emergence of the H3N2 subclade K (J.2.4.1) with multiple antigenically relevant mutations. Using an immunoinformatics-driven approach, the authors designed a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV) targeting the HA protein of this variant, incorporating lineage-specific mutations and selecting epitopes based on antigenicity, non-allergenicity, and immunogenic potential. The final MEV construct showed favorable physicochemical properties, structural stability, and stable interactions with TLR4 in silico. Immune simulations predicted effective humoral and cellular responses with immunological memory. While these computational findings suggest enhanced strain-specific immune recognition, the authors emphasize the need for experimental validation to confirm immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy, indicating a moderate strength of evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于血凝素 (HA) 糖蛋白中 进化 的快速抗原性,流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 造成了持续的公共卫生挑战,这经常破坏 疫苗 的有效性。具有多个抗原相关 突变 的 H3N2 亚支 K (J.2.4.1) 的出现需要更新的 疫苗 策略,能够引发毒株特异性 免疫应答。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用免疫信息学驱动的方法来设计针对 H3N2 亚进化枝 K (J.2.4.1) 变体的 HA 蛋白的多表位 疫苗 (MEV)。疫苗 构建体纳入了谱系特异性 突变,并对其理化性质、结构稳定性和 免疫应答 潜力进行了评估。
elements_zh.methods: HA 序列被修改为包括谱系特异性 突变,并使用 NetMHCpan/NetMHCIIpan 算法和 IEDB 平台预测细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞 (CTL)、辅助 T 淋巴细胞 (HTL) 和 B 细胞表位。根据抗原性、非过敏性、无毒性和免疫原性潜力选择高置信度表位,然后与接头和 50S 核糖体蛋白 L7/L12 佐剂组装。
elements_zh.main_results: 最终的 MEV 构建体表现出良好的物理化学特性、结构稳定性和令人满意的模型验证。分子对接和动力学模拟显示与 TLR4 的稳定相互作用,而免疫模拟则预测了具有免疫记忆生成的有效体液和细胞 免疫应答。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为表明将 J.2.4.1 特异性抗原 疫苗 纳入 MEV 可能会增强毒株特异性免疫识别,为快速下一代流感 疫苗 开发提供有前景的计算框架。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项研究提供了一种计算策略,用于设计针对新兴变异的菌株特异性流感 疫苗,可能为未来的 监测 和 疫苗 菌株选择提供信息,以提高 疫苗 针对 H3N2 亚支 K 的有效性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于计算预测和模拟,作者明确指出需要实验验证来确认免疫原性、安全性和保护功效,这表明证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.main_results: 最终的 MEV 构建体表现出良好的物理化学特性、结构稳定性和令人满意的模型验证。分子对接和动力学模拟显示与 TLR4 的稳定相互作用,而免疫模拟则预测了具有免疫记忆生成的有效体液和细胞 免疫应答。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为表明将 J.2.4.1 特异性抗原 疫苗 纳入 MEV 可能会增强毒株特异性免疫识别,为快速下一代流感 疫苗 开发提供有前景的计算框架。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项研究提供了一种计算策略,用于设计针对新兴变异的菌株特异性流感 疫苗,可能为未来的 监测 和 疫苗 菌株选择提供信息,以提高 疫苗 针对 H3N2 亚支 K 的有效性。

papers.title: Determinants of the Seasonal Influenza Vaccination Uptake Among People Aged 50 Years or Above During and After the Pandemic: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Seasonal influenza vaccination (SIV) coverage remains suboptimal among adults aged ≥50 years, and the COVID-19 pandemic might influence the determinants of SIV uptake. This systematic review aimed to identify determinants of SIV uptake among adults aged ≥50 years during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods: We searched PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Global Health, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, APA PsycINFO, and APA PsycArticles for studies published between 1 December 2019 and 1 January 2026. The pooled prevalence of SIV uptake was synthesized using random-effects models in meta-analysis. Results: A total of 50 studies were included in the systematic review. COVID-19-related factors, such as perceived risk of co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and seasonal influenza and concerns about potential interactions between COVID-19 vaccines and SIV, were determinants of SIV uptake. Other modifiable determinants included those that existed before the pandemic (e.g., knowledge and perceptions of seasonal influenza and SIV). Subgroup analysis showed that cost and inaccessibility were barriers to receiving SIV in places without a fully subsidized SIV, and perceived susceptibility and vaccine safety concerns were commonly identified as facilitators and barriers in studies with data collected after the pandemic. The pooled prevalence of SIV uptake among adults aged 50 years or above was 53% (95% confidence interval: 44–62%). Such uptake appeared lower among adults aged 50–64 years, in regions without a fully subsidized SIV, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Conclusions: These findings could inform service planning and interventions promoting SIV uptake among adults aged ≥50 years in the post-pandemic era. More studies are needed to explore determinants specific to people aged 50–64 years to inform health promotion tailored to their needs.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines the determinants of seasonal influenza vaccination (SIV) uptake among adults aged ≥50 years during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The review included 50 studies and found that the pooled prevalence of SIV uptake was 53% (95% confidence interval: 44–62%). Key determinants included perceived risk of co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and seasonal influenza, as well as concerns about interactions between vaccines. Barriers such as cost and inaccessibility were more prevalent in regions without fully subsidized SIV programs. The review highlights the need for targeted health promotion strategies, especially for adults aged 50–64 years, to improve vaccination rates in the post-pandemic era.

papers.abstract: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện năm 2025 bằng phương pháp chọn mẫu thuận tiện trên 280 kháchhàng đến Phòng Tiêm chủng Trường Đại học Y Hà Nội nhằm mô tả kiến thức, thực hành về tiêm vắc xinphòng bệnh cúm mùa và phân tích một số yếu tố liên quan. Kết quả cho thấy 44,3% đối tượng có kiến thứctốt và 40,4% đã tiêm vắc xin cúm mùa trong vòng 12 tháng qua. Phân tích hồi quy logistic đơn biến ghinhận kiến thức có liên quan với tuổi >30 (OR = 1,84; KTC95%: 1,11–3,05), trình độ học vấn (sơ cấp/ trungcấp/ cao đẳng: OR = 3,07; KTC95%: 1,14–8,62; đại học/sau đại học: OR = 2,28; KTC95%: 1,07–8,60), đãkết hôn (OR = 1,68; KTC95%: 1,01–2,85) và thu nhập 15–20 triệu đồng/ tháng (OR = 2,72; KTC95%: 1,21–6,34). Thực hành tiêm vắc xin cúm mùa có liên quan với nơi cư trú (ngoại thành: OR = 0,23; KTC95%:0,07–0,67; ngoài tỉnh: OR = 0,53; KTC95%: 0,30–0,93), nghề nghiệp (hành chính/văn phòng: OR = 2,19;KTC95%: 1,12–4,40; hưu trí/nội trợ: OR = 4,15; KTC95%: 1,56–11,53) và đã kết hôn (OR = 2,10; KTC95%:1,20–3,57). Tỷ lệ kiến thức tốt và thực hành tiêm vắc xin cúm mùa còn chưa cao. Cần tăng cường truyềnthông, tư vấn nhằm nâng cao nhận thức và thúc đẩy thực hành tiêm chủng tại cơ sở.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed low uptake and knowledge gaps regarding seasonal influenza vaccination among clients attending a university vaccination center in Hanoi in 2025, aiming to describe knowledge and practices and identify associated factors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 using convenience sampling of 280 clients attending the vaccination center of Hanoi Medical University to assess knowledge and practices about seasonal influenza vaccination.
analysis.methods: The study used convenience sampling and descriptive analysis to evaluate knowledge and vaccination practices, with logistic regression to identify factors associated with knowledge and practice outcomes.
analysis.main_results: Good knowledge was reported by 44.3% of participants, and 40.4% had received seasonal influenza vaccine within the past 12 months. Knowledge was associated with age over 30 years, lower education levels, being married, and monthly income of 15–20 million Vietnamese dong.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that knowledge and vaccination practices remain suboptimal and identified demographic and socioeconomic factors influencing both knowledge and vaccination behavior.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest targeted communication and counseling are needed to improve seasonal influenza vaccination uptake and knowledge among specific demographic groups in Hanoi.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design and convenience sampling limit causal inference and generalizability; evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to potential selection bias and unmeasured confounders.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study conducted in 2025 at Hanoi Medical University assessed knowledge and practices regarding seasonal influenza vaccination among 280 clients using convenience sampling. It found that 44.3% had good knowledge and 40.4% had received the vaccine in the past year. Knowledge was associated with age over 30 years, lower education levels, being married, and higher income, while vaccination practice was linked to residence, occupation, and marital status. The authors concluded that knowledge and vaccination rates remain insufficient and recommended targeted communication to improve uptake. The study’s moderate evidence strength reflects its cross-sectional design and convenience sampling, which limit causal inference and generalizability.

papers.abstract: Tiêm vắc xin cúm là cách hiệu quả nhất để ngăn ngừa và kiểm soát bệnh cúm mùa. Nghiên cứu cắt ngangvới phương pháp chọn mẫu thuận tiện triển khai trên 205 người từ 50 tuổi trở lên nhằm mô tả thực trạngkiến thức, thực hành về tiêm vắc xin phòng bệnh cúm mùa của người lớn tuổi tại xã Bình Giang tỉnh NinhBình. Kết quả nghiên cứu chỉ ra rằng có 62,9% đối tượng có kiến thức đạt về bệnh cúm mùa và vắc xinphòng bệnh; 20,9% đối tượng đã tiêm vắc xin cúm mùa năm 2025. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to assess the current knowledge and vaccination practices regarding seasonal influenza vaccine among adults aged 50 years and older in Binh Giang Commune, responding to the recognized importance of influenza vaccination as the most effective means to prevent seasonal flu.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross‐sectional convenience sample of 205 adults aged 50 years and older was implemented in Binh Giang Commune, Ninh Binh Province, Vietnam, to describe their knowledge and vaccination practices.
analysis.methods: Data were collected through a convenience sampling cross‐sectional survey measuring knowledge and vaccination status via self‐report.
analysis.main_results: The survey found that 62.9% of participants had adequate knowledge of seasonal influenza and its vaccine, while only 20.9% reported receiving the seasonal influenza vaccine in 2025.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These results reveal a substantial knowledge–action gap, indicating that despite high knowledge, vaccination uptake remains low among older adults in this setting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The main barriers—lack of awareness, limited access to vaccination sites, and high cost—highlight the need for intensified communication, improved vaccine accessibility, and supportive vaccination programs to boost seasonal influenza vaccination in this community.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The convenience sampling and single‐site design limit generalisability, and the absence of a comparison group reduces the evidence strength to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This cross‐sectional study surveyed 205 adults aged 50 years and older in Binh Giang Commune, Ninh Binh Province, Vietnam, in 2025 to evaluate knowledge and vaccination practices against seasonal influenza. Results showed that 62.9% of participants possessed adequate knowledge of seasonal flu and its vaccine, yet only 20.9% had received the seasonal influenza vaccine during the year. The principal barriers to vaccination were lack of awareness (28.2%), limited access to vaccination sites (24.5%), and high cost (16.0%). These findings indicate a substantial knowledge‐action gap that underscores the need for targeted public‐health communication, improved vaccine accessibility, and supportive vaccination programs to increase uptake among older adults. The convenience sampling design and single‐site approach limit the generalisability of the results, but the data provide moderate‐quality evidence on current vaccination behavior and barriers in this community.

papers.title: Investigating host intracellular proteins with antiviral activity against influenza and herpesviruses
papers.abstract: Human pathogenic viruses present an ongoing global public health problem, as reflected by continuing endemic infections, seasonal epidemics, and pandemics caused by newly emerging viruses. While many intracellular host proteins fulfil defined roles in normal cellular physiology and function, a subset exert intrinsic antiviral activity and are termed host restriction factors. Host restriction factors represent an important component of innate antiviral immunity and can inhibit infection and/or replication of different DNA and/or RNA viruses at distinct stages in their viral replication cycle. This thesis has focussed on studying how two host restriction factors, namely SAM domain and HD domain-containing protein 1 (SAMHD1) and Membrane-associated RING-CH-Type Finger 8 protein (MARCHF8), restrict different RNA and DNA viruses. Studies described in Chapter 3 investigated the antiviral activity of SAMHD1 against respiratory RNA viruses in human macrophage-like and epithelial cells. Using human herpes simplex type 1 virus (HSV-1) as a control to validate the functionality of our approaches, we demonstrated that neither endogenous nor overexpressed SAMHD restricted seasonal influenza A virus (IAV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV) and human parainfluenza virus type 3 (hPIV3) replication in either cell type. However, overexpression of SAMHD1 inhibited highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAI) A(H5N1) in human macrophage-like cells. HSV-1 infects a wide range of cell types, including epithelial cells, keratinocytes, astrocytes, neurons and immune cells, yet most studies published to date have investigated the role of SAMHD1 in restricting HSV-1 replication in monocytes and macrophages. In Chapter 4, we focussed on assessment of SAMHD1 expression and its role in restricting HSV-1 replication in different cell types relevant to HSV-1 pathogenesis, including keratinocytes, neurons and astrocytes. We report that endogenous SAMHD1 did not restrict HSV-1 replication in any of the neuron, astrocyte or keratinocyte cell models tested, whereas restriction was observed in differentiated THP-1 macrophages. In contrast, inducible overexpression of SAMHD1 in neuronal, but not in keratinocyte cell lines, resulted in HSV-1 restriction, with variable results observed following overexpression in an astrocytic cell line. We also used human small molecule neural precursor cells (smNPCs), derived from human pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and differentiated into neurons or astrocytes, to confirm that endogenous SAMHD1 did not restrict HSV-1 replication in either cell type. Together, these results indicate that the capacity of both endogenous and overexpressed SAMHD1 to restrict HSV-1 replication is cell-type dependent. We extended our studies of human SAMHD1 and herpesviruses to investigate the ability of bovine SAMHD1 to restrict replication of human and bovine herpesviruses (Chapter 5). We used an inducible overexpression system to express bovine SAMHD1 and, for comparison, human SAMHD1 in bovine epithelial- and macrophage-like cells, enabling assessment of their ability to restrict bovine herpesvirus type 1 (BHV-1) replication. We demonstrate that inducible expression of either bovine or human SAMHD1 restricted the replication of BHV-1, as well as HSV-1. Restriction of BHV-1 by bovine SAMHD1 correlated with the inhibition of viral genomic replication and late viral gene expression. Furthermore, by introducing mutations known to impact the nuclear localisation, dNTPase activity or antiviral activity against lentiviruses, we show that only dNTPase activity was required for restriction of BHV-1 by bovine SAMHD1. In Chapter 6, we report the ability of MARCHF8 to restrict HSV-1 replication in macrophage- or epithelial-like cells. While it is widely established that MARCHF8 can restrict replication of several RNA viruses, this represents the first report of its ability to act against a DNA virus. For many RNA viruses, MARCHF8-mediated restriction has been associated with downregulation of viral envelope glycoproteins from the cell surface, thereby limiting their subsequent incorporation into nascent virions. However, while MARCHF8 expression did not affect virus entry, translocation of viral genome to the nucleus and immediate early (IE) gene expression, it did inhibit HSV-1 genomic replication, and therefore subsequent late viral gene expression and release of infectious virions. MARCHF8-mediated restriction of HSV-1 occurred independent of other cellular factors known to impact genomic replication of HSV-1, namely SAMHD1 and CD81, and could also proceed efficiently in cells expressing a functional cGAS-STING pathway. To our knowledge, these studies are the first to demonstrate MARCHF8-mediated restriction of a human DNA virus. Moreover, inhibition of HSV-1 genomic replication represents a novel mechanism of MARCHF8-mediated virus restriction that is distinct to its reported antiviral activity against RNA viruses. Overall, our studies indicate that SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 represent broad-spectrum host restriction factors with the ability to act across different classes of viruses with distinct viral genomes, likely via mechanisms distinct to those previously described. Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential of bovine SAMHD1 to restrict replication of BHV-1, a bovine herpesvirus associated with significant economic impact in the cattle industry. Targeting host restriction factors such as SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 represents a promising approach for the development of novel host-directed antiviral therapies.

papers.title_original: Investigating host intracellular proteins with antiviral activity against influenza and herpesviruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: Seasonal influenza viruses cause recurring epidemics and remain a global public health burden, yet the role of host restriction factors in controlling these infections is incompletely understood. This thesis aimed to investigate how host restriction factors SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 restrict influenza and herpesviruses, addressing a gap in understanding their antiviral breadth and mechanisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examined the antiviral activity of SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 in human and bovine cell models, including macrophage-like, epithelial, neuronal, astrocytic, and keratinocyte cells, using inducible overexpression systems and endogenous protein assessments. The work was structured across multiple chapters, each focusing on specific virus-host interactions.
analysis.methods: Inducible overexpression systems were used to express SAMHD1 (human and bovine) and MARCHF8 in relevant cell types, enabling assessment of their ability to restrict viral replication. For SAMHD1, mutations affecting nuclear localisation, dNTPase activity, or lentiviral antiviral activity were introduced to dissect functional requirements. Viral replication was measured by assessing genomic replication, gene expression, and infectious virion release.
analysis.main_results: Neither endogenous nor overexpressed human SAMHD1 restricted seasonal influenza A virus (IAV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV), or human parainfluenza virus type 3 (hPIV3) replication in macrophage-like or epithelial cells. Overexpression of SAMHD1 inhibited highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in human macrophage-like cells. Endogenous SAMHD1 did not restrict HSV-1 in neurons, astrocytes, or keratinocytes, though restriction was observed in differentiated THP-1 macrophages.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that SAMHD1 does not restrict seasonal influenza viruses but retains activity against highly pathogenic avian influenza, highlighting virus-specific differences in restriction factor efficacy. The finding that MARCHF8 restricts HSV-1 via inhibition of genomic replication represents a novel mechanism distinct from its known activity against RNA viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that host restriction factors may have limited direct impact on seasonal influenza control in common human cell types, while informing potential strategies to target highly pathogenic avian influenza. The evidence is moderate, as the absence of restriction against seasonal influenza is based on negative results in specific cell types, and broader generalisability remains uncertain.

analysis.summary_en: This thesis investigated the antiviral activity of host restriction factors SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 against influenza and herpesviruses. Using inducible overexpression and endogenous protein assessments in human and bovine cell models, the study found that neither endogenous nor overexpressed human SAMHD1 restricted seasonal influenza A virus (IAV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV), or human parainfluenza virus type 3 (hPIV3) in macrophage-like or epithelial cells. However, SAMHD1 overexpression inhibited highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in human macrophage-like cells, indicating virus-specific differences in restriction factor efficacy. Endogenous SAMHD1 did not restrict herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) in neurons, astrocytes, or keratinocytes, though restriction was observed in differentiated THP-1 macrophages. The study also demonstrated that MARCHF8 restricts HSV-1 by inhibiting genomic replication, a novel mechanism distinct from its known activity against RNA viruses. These findings suggest limited direct impact of SAMHD1 on seasonal influenza in common human cell types, while highlighting potential for targeting highly pathogenic avian influenza and expanding the antiviral spectrum of MARCHF8.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 季节性流感 病毒引起反复流行,并仍然是全球公共卫生负担,但 宿主 限制因素在控制这些感染中的作用尚不完全清楚。本论文旨在研究 宿主 限制因子 SAMHD1 和 MARCHF8 如何限制流感和疱疹病毒,弥补对其 抗病毒药物 广度和机制的理解空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用诱导型过表达系统和内源性蛋白质评估,检测了 SAMHD1 和 MARCHF8 在人和牛细胞模型中的 抗病毒药物 活性,包括巨噬细胞样细胞、上皮细胞、神经元细胞、星形细胞和角质形成细胞。这项工作由多个章节组成,每个章节都侧重于特定的病毒-宿主 相互作用。

papers.title: CD73 controls neutrophil responsiveness to type I interferon impairing antibacterial responses during influenza A virus/ Streptococcus pneumoniae co-infection
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus) are asymptomatic colonizers of the nasopharynx but can progress to pulmonary and systemic pathogens upon influenza A virus (IAV) infection. Polymorphonuclear cells (PMNs) are required to control bacterial numbers, but we previously found that IAV infection impairs their ability to kill S. Here, using a model that allows transition of pneumococci from colonizers to disease-causing pathogens upon IAV co-infection, we examined the signaling pathways impairing PMN responses. When we investigated the effect of type I interferons (IFN) produced upon IAV infection on PMN antibacterial activity, we found that PMNs treated with IFN were unable to kill S. pneumoniae ex vivo, and that in vivo blocking of IFN receptor 1 (IFNAR1) in IAV infected mice rescued PMN antibacterial function. In exploring what controls PMN responsiveness to IFN, we examined CD73, an ectonucleotidase that is known to regulate PMN function in primary pneumococcal pneumonia. To test if there is an intersection between CD73 and IFN signaling, we examined receptor levels and IFN production in wild type versus CD73KO mice and found no difference in IFNAR expression on PMNs or IFNɑ and IFNꞵ levels in the lungs and circulation. However, CD73KO PMNs expressed significantly lower levels of the interferon stimulated protein IFIT1. When we looked at ex vivo PMN responsiveness to IFNs, CD73KO PMNs were less responsive to IFN-mediated inhibition of antimicrobial activity. In exploring mechanisms, we found that CD73 expressing PMNs had elevated production of reactive oxygen species in response to IAV challenge, that paradoxically impaired their ability to kill S. Importantly, despite similar pathogen loads in the respiratory tract, co-infected CD73KO mice cleared bacteremia and survived significantly better than wild type controls. These findings suggest that CD73 impairs host defense against IAV/S. pneumoniae co-infection in part by sensitizing PMNs to type I IFN-mediated inhibition of antibacterial function.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how influenza A virus (IAV) infection affects the ability of polymorphonuclear cells (PMNs) to combat Streptococcus pneumoniae, particularly focusing on the role of type I interferons (IFN) in this process.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how influenza A virus (IAV) infection affects the ability of polymorphonuclear cells (PMNs) to combat Streptococcus pneumoniae, particularly focusing on the role of type I interferons (IFN). Using a model where pneumococci transition from colonizers to pathogens upon IAV co-infection, the researchers examined the signaling pathways that impair PMN responses. They found that PMNs treated with IFN were unable to kill S. pneumoniae ex vivo, and in vivo blocking of IFN receptor 1 (IFNAR1) in IAV-infected mice rescued PMN antibacterial function. Additionally, CD73KO PMNs expressed significantly lower levels of the interferon stimulated protein IFIT1. These findings suggest that CD73 impairs host defense against IAV/S. pneumoniae co-infection by sensitizing PMNs to type I IFN-mediated inhibition of antibacterial function. The results highlight the importance of understanding the interplay between viral and bacterial infections in the context of immune response modulation, which could inform strategies for improving treatment and prevention in co-infected patients. However, the study is limited to ex vivo and in vivo models, and the evidence is based on a single model system, which may affect generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查甲型流感病毒(IAV)感染如何影响多形核细胞(PMN)对抗肺炎链球菌的能力,特别关注I型干扰素(IFN)在此过程中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了肺炎球菌在 IAV 合并感染时从定植者转变为病原体的模型,检查了在这种情况下损害 PMN 反应的信号通路。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员研究了 IAV 感染期间产生的 I 型干扰素对 PMN 抗菌活性的影响,比较野生型和 CD73KO 小鼠以评估受体水平和 IFN 产生。
elements_zh.main_results: 用 IFN 处理的 PMN 无法离体杀死肺炎链球菌,而体内阻断 IAV 感染小鼠的 IFN 受体 1 (IFNAR1) 可挽救 PMN 的抗菌功能。CD73KO PMN 的干扰素刺激蛋白 IFIT1 表达水平显着降低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明 CD73 削弱了 宿主 对 IAV/S 的防御。通过使 PMN 对 I 型 IFN 介导的抗菌功能抑制敏感来治疗肺炎链球菌合并感染。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果提供了对 IAV 感染损害 宿主 对细菌合并感染的防御机制的见解,这可以为改善 治疗 和合并感染患者的预防策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于离体和体内模型,证据基于单一模型系统,这可能会影响普遍性。证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 肺炎链球菌(肺炎球菌)是鼻咽部的无症状定植菌,但在甲型流感病毒(IAV)感染后可发展为肺部和全身病原体。控制细菌数量需要多形核细胞(PMN),但我们之前发现 IAV 感染会损害它们杀死链球菌的能力。在这里,我们使用一种模型,允许肺炎球菌在 IAV 共同感染时从定植者转变为致病病原体,检查了损害 PMN 反应的信号通路。当我们研究 IAV 感染后产生的 I 型干扰素 (IFN) 对 PMN 抗菌活性的影响时,我们发现用 IFN 处理的 PMN 无法离体杀死肺炎链球菌,而体内阻断 IAV 感染小鼠的 IFN 受体 1 (IFNAR1) 可以挽救 PMN 的抗菌功能。在探索控制 PMN 对 IFN 反应性的过程中,我们检测了 CD73,这是一种已知可调节原发性肺炎球菌肺炎中 PMN 功能的核酸外切酶。为了测试 CD73 和 IFN 信号传导之间是否存在交叉,我们检查了野生型与 CD73KO 小鼠的受体水平和 IFN 产生,发现 PMN 上的 IFNAR 表达或肺部和循环中的 IFNɑ 和 IFNꞵ 水平没有差异。然而,CD73KO PMN 的干扰素刺激蛋白 IFIT1 表达水平显着降低。当我们观察体外 PMN 对 IFN 的反应时,CD73KO PMN 对 IFN 介导的抗菌活性抑制反应较差。在探索机制时,我们发现表达 CD73 的 PMN 在应对 IAV 攻击时活性氧的产生增加,这反而损害了它们杀死链球菌的能力。重要的是,尽管呼吸道中的病原体负荷相似,但共感染的 CD73KO 小鼠清除菌血症的能力和存活率明显优于野生型对照小鼠。这些发现表明 CD73 损害 宿主 对 IAV/S 的防御。肺炎链球菌合并感染的部分原因是使 PMN 对 I 型 IFN 介导的抗菌功能抑制敏感。

papers.title: Molecular Surveillance and Nanopore Sequencing Reveal the Circulation and Genetic Diversity of Low-Pathogenic Avian Influenza A Viruses in Migratory Birds from Ukraine
papers.abstract: Wild migratory birds are the principal natural reservoir of influenza A viruses (IAVs) and play a central role in their evolution and global dissemination. Ukraine lies along the Black Sea–Mediterranean Flyway, making surveillance of avian influenza viruses in wild birds essential within a One Health framework, although genomic data from the region remain limited. Between October 2025 and January 2026 In some places you say December 2025 and in other places you say January 2026. I do not understand the differences, 604 cloacal and oropharyngeal swabs and environmental fecal samples were collected from migratory birds and mixed-species flocks in the Tuzlivski lymany National Nature Park and surrounding areas, together with samples from nearby domestic poultry. Influenza A virus was detected by real-time RT-PCR targeting the matrix gene, followed by H5/H7 screening, Oxford Nanopore sequencing of complete hemagglutinin genes, and phylogenetic analysis. Influenza A virus RNA was identified in 30/604 samples (4.97%), whereas all samples were negative for H5 and H7 subtypes. Complete hemagglutinin sequences revealed three low-pathogenic subtypes (H1, H4, and H6) that clustered within established Eurasian lineages closely related to contemporary avian viruses circulating across Europe, Asia, and North America. No influenza A virus or Newcastle disease virus was detected in domestic poultry. These findings provide an important genomic baseline for avian influenza surveillance in Ukraine and demonstrate the value of portable nanopore sequencing and integrated One Health surveillance for monitoring viral diversity and supporting early detection of emerging influenza threats.

analysis.summary_en: This correction addresses errors in a previously published study on the interaction of RNA G-quadruplexes from influenza A virus vRNA with TMPyP4 and BRACO-19 ligands. papers.title: Recent advances in emerging approaches for influenza a detection
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a major focus of global public health concern, as it can cause influenza-like illness and severe respiratory infections. Therefore, achieving accurate and sensitive detection of IAV would greatly facilitate disease diagnosis and control. The two main conventional technical methods for IAV detection that are reviewed in this article are viral nucleic acid amplification analysis and immunological assays. At the same time, this review pays special attention to the cross-integration of these two types of techniques with modern engineering technologies, and systematically introduces novel biosensors (offering significantly enhanced sensitivity) and point-of-care testing (POCT) devices (enabling rapid on-site diagnosis) developed based on these two principles. However, it is important to note that the majority of these novel platforms remain at the proof-of-concept stage, with validation largely confined to laboratory settings. By delineating the current state of these technologies, this review identifies key challenges and future directions for translating research innovations into clinical practice.
