papers.title: Early oseltamivir initiation and influenza outcomes in kidney transplant recipients: a multicenter real-world study
papers.abstract: Influenza infection poses a significant clinical threat to kidney transplant recipients due to their immunocompromised status. Although current guidelines recommend early antiviral therapy, real-world evidence supporting the effectiveness of oseltamivir, particularly regarding the optimal timing of initiation in this vulnerable population remains scarce. To identify independent factors associated with clinical improvement and time to symptom resolution in kidney transplant recipients infected with the influenza virus and treated with oseltamivir. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study enrolling adult kidney transplant recipients diagnosed with influenza virus infection across five centers between October 2023 and March 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using a validated Composite Symptom Score (range: 0–21) based on seven typical influenza symptoms. Clinical improvement was defined as achieving a score of ≤ 1 on the fifth day after oseltamivir initiation. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with clinical improvement, and linear regression was used to evaluate factors influencing time to symptom resolution. Given the small number of events, the multivariable logistic model was estimated using Firth’s penalized likelihood method and restricted to two core predictors. A total of 58 kidney transplant recipients were included. After one course of oseltamivir, 46 patients (79.3%) achieved clinical improvement. Compared with the improved group, patients without improvement had a significantly lower rate of early oseltamivir initiation (≤ 48 h: 58.3% vs. 84.8%, P = 0.044) and tended to present with higher baseline symptom scores. analysis.summary_en: This multicenter retrospective study evaluated the impact of early oseltamivir initiation on clinical outcomes in 58 kidney transplant recipients with influenza across five centers from October 2023 to March 2024. Using a validated Composite Symptom Score, 79.3% of patients achieved clinical improvement after treatment, with early initiation (≤ 48 hours) independently associated with higher odds of improvement (adjusted OR 0.16) and shorter symptom resolution (β 5.02). Late treatment initiation and higher baseline severity were linked to poorer outcomes. The study provides real-world evidence supporting guideline recommendations for prompt antiviral therapy in this immunocompromised population, though limitations include a small sample size and retrospective design that constrain generalizability.

papers.title: Socioeconomic differences in influenza vaccination coverage by government financial support status: A population-based study in Korea
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza can be prevented through vaccination, however vaccination coverage remains low. This study aims to analyze whether government financial support policies associated with improved vaccination coverage and to further analyze other influencing socioeconomic factors. METHODS: This study utilized secondary data from the 2020 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey to analyze factors influencing influenza vaccination among 5,592 participants. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to analyze the association between government financial support and vaccination coverage, and to analyze socioeconomic factors influencing vaccination in both the government-supported and non-supported groups. RESULTS: The vaccination rate was higher in the financial-supported group(63.8%) than in the non-supported group(33.1%). After adjustment, the financial assistance group had a 2.02 higher vaccination coverage compared to the non-supported group. In the financial-supported group, low education and economic inactivity were associated with higher vaccination rates. While, in the non-supported group, women, higher household-income, and having employee-insured subscribers were associated with vaccination coverage. CONCLUSIONS: Financial support is provided to high-risk groups for influenza infection, and this group showed higher vaccination coverage in low socioeconomic groups. Therefore, targeted government intervention appears necessary to improve vaccination coverage in high-risk groups.

papers.title: Influenza-Associated Cardiac Manifestations: A Systematic Review of Case Reports and Case Series
papers.abstract: Background: Influenza is primarily a respiratory illness, but it is increasingly linked to acute cardiovascular complications, including myocarditis and sudden cardiac death. Evidence on influenza-associated cardiac involvement remains fragmented and largely derived from case-based reports. Methods: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251249130). PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for eligible studies. Case reports and case series were included to characterize rare, severe, or atypical cardiac manifestations that are not captured in larger epidemiological studies. Data on demographics, influenza subtype, cardiac manifestations, investigations, management, and outcomes were extracted. Results: Thirty-three studies (32 case reports and one case series) comprising 36 cases were included. Influenza A was reported in 26 cases and influenza B was reported in 9 cases. Myocarditis was the most common manifestation (19 cases, 53%), including fulminant myocarditis in 9 cases (25%). Cardiogenic shock occurred in seven cases (19%), malignant arrhythmias in four(11%), myocardial infarction–like presentations in three (8%), and cardiac arrest or sudden cardiac death in six cases (17%). Cardiac involvement occurred across all age groups, frequently in patients without pre-existing coronary artery disease. Overall mortality was 44% (16/36), with fatalities reported in both influenza A and B infections. These findings predominantly reflect severe and published cases and may not represent the full clinical spectrum of influenza-associated cardiac involvement. Conclusions: This review highlights that influenza infection has been reported in association with a range of acute cardiac manifestations, particularly myocarditis, including severe and fulminant presentations. However, given the reliance on case reports and case series, the findings are subject to significant publication bias and do not permit the estimation of incidence, risk, or causal inference. These observations should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating.

papers.title_zh: 流感相关心脏表现:病例报告 和病例系列的系统评价
papers.source_body_en: Background: Influenza is primarily a respiratory illness, but it is increasingly linked to acute cardiovascular complications, including myocarditis and sudden cardiac death. Evidence on influenza-associated cardiac involvement remains fragmented and largely derived from case-based reports. Methods: This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251249130). PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for eligible studies. Case reports and case series were included to characterize rare, severe, or atypical cardiac manifestations that are not captured in larger epidemiological studies. Data on demographics, influenza subtype, cardiac manifestations, investigations, management, and outcomes were extracted. Results: Thirty-three studies (32 case reports and one case series) comprising 36 cases were included. Influenza A was reported in 26 cases and influenza B was reported in 9 cases. Myocarditis was the most common manifestation (19 cases, 53%), including fulminant myocarditis in 9 cases (25%). Cardiogenic shock occurred in seven cases (19%), malignant arrhythmias in four(11%), myocardial infarction–like presentations in three (8%), and cardiac arrest or sudden cardiac death in six cases (17%). Cardiac involvement occurred across all age groups, frequently in patients without pre-existing coronary artery disease. Overall mortality was 44% (16/36), with fatalities reported in both influenza A and B infections. These findings predominantly reflect severe and published cases and may not represent the full clinical spectrum of influenza-associated cardiac involvement. Conclusions: This review highlights that influenza infection has been reported in association with a range of acute cardiac manifestations, particularly myocarditis, including severe and fulminant presentations. However, given the reliance on case reports and case series, the findings are subject to significant publication bias and do not permit the estimation of incidence, risk, or causal inference. These observations should therefore be interpreted as hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: APP and APLP2 Kunitz Domains Are Potent Endogenous Inhibitors of TMPRSS2 and Respiratory Virus Infection
papers.abstract: Respiratory viruses depend on host proteases for activation of viral fusion proteins, making these enzymes attractive targets for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. We previously identified Trypstatin, a human Bikunin-derived Kunitz domain, as a potent endogenous inhibitor of the airway serine protease TMPRSS2. Here, we investigated whether TMPRSS2 inhibition is shared by additional human Kunitz domains. Kunitz domains with high sequence similarity to Trypstatin were synthesized, refolded, and functionally characterized. Domains derived from amyloid precursor protein (APP) and amyloid precursor-like protein 2 (APLP2) potently inhibited TMPRSS2, with APP displaying subnanomolar activity comparable to camostat mesylate. APP and APLP2 selectively blocked SARS-CoV-2 Spike-mediated entry without affecting VSV-G-mediated entry or cell viability and inhibited infection by multiple coronaviruses and influenza viruses, but not TMPRSS2-independent rhinovirus. In primary human airway epithelial cultures, APP and Trypstatin reduced replication of SARS-CoV-2, endemic coronaviruses, and influenza A virus, and remained stable in airway mucus. These findings identify APP and APLP2 Kunitz domains as potent endogenous inhibitors of TMPRSS2-dependent respiratory virus infection and promising scaffolds for host-directed broad-spectrum antivirals.

analysis.methods: Kunitz domains with high sequence similarity to Trypstatin were synthesized, refolded, and functionally characterized. The domains were tested for their ability to inhibit TMPRSS2 and prevent respiratory virus infection in human airway epithelial cultures.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that APP and APLP2 Kunitz domains could be used to develop new antiviral strategies targeting TMPRSS2, which may have implications for the treatment and prevention of seasonal influenza viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates whether Kunitz domains from APP and APLP2 can inhibit TMPRSS2, a host protease critical for respiratory virus activation. The research builds on previous findings that Trypstatin, a Kunitz domain derived from Bikunin, is a potent inhibitor of TMPRSS2. The authors synthesized and functionally characterized Kunitz domains with high sequence similarity to Trypstatin, revealing that APP and APLP2 domains potently inhibit TMPRSS2. These domains effectively blocked SARS-CoV-2 Spike-mediated entry without affecting cell viability and inhibited infection by multiple coronaviruses and influenza viruses. The study highlights the potential of APP and APLP2 Kunitz domains as endogenous inhibitors of TMPRSS2-dependent respiratory virus infection, offering promising scaffolds for broad-spectrum antiviral development. The findings are based on abstract-only evidence, which limits their depth but supports moderate confidence in their conclusions.

papers.title_zh: APP 和 APLP2 Kunitz 结构域是 TMPRSS2 和呼吸道病毒感染的有效内源抑制剂
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory viruses depend on host proteases for activation of viral fusion proteins, making these enzymes attractive targets for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies. We previously identified Trypstatin, a human Bikunin-derived Kunitz domain, as a potent endogenous inhibitor of the airway serine protease TMPRSS2. Here, we investigated whether TMPRSS2 inhibition is shared by additional human Kunitz domains. Kunitz domains with high sequence similarity to Trypstatin were synthesized, refolded, and functionally characterized. Domains derived from amyloid precursor protein (APP) and amyloid precursor-like protein 2 (APLP2) potently inhibited TMPRSS2, with APP displaying subnanomolar activity comparable to camostat mesylate. APP and APLP2 selectively blocked SARS-CoV-2 Spike-mediated entry without affecting VSV-G-mediated entry or cell viability and inhibited infection by multiple coronaviruses and influenza viruses, but not TMPRSS2-independent rhinovirus. In primary human airway epithelial cultures, APP and Trypstatin reduced replication of SARS-CoV-2, endemic coronaviruses, and influenza A virus, and remained stable in airway mucus. These findings identify APP and APLP2 Kunitz domains as potent endogenous inhibitors of TMPRSS2-dependent respiratory virus infection and promising scaffolds for host-directed broad-spectrum antivirals.

news.content_title: Kinney Drugs opens seasonal flu vaccine appointments
news.content: Gene Morse Updated Tue, August 4, 2026 at 3:38 PM UTC 0 GOUVERNEUR, N.Y. (WWTI) – Kinney Drugs has opened seasonal flu vaccination appointments in all its pharmacies. Kinney Drugs has vaccines on hand, available for those ages 2-64 in New York; 3-64 in Vermont; and High-dose vaccines for seniors age 65+. For the 2026-2027 season, flu vaccines are a trivalent formulation offering protection against three flu viruses: A/H1N1; A/H3N2; and B/Victoria Lineage. The new H3N2 component was selected to better address a subclade of the virus that was predominant during the 25/26 season. Influenza vaccines are reviewed and reformulated annually to address currently circulating strains of the virus. Appointments can be scheduled at the Kinney Drugs website or by using the Kinney Drugs app. When booking online: Find the “ Pharmacy ” tab; Click to “ Vaccines and Immunizations ”; and Select from the menu. A list of stores is available on the website, or you may search by zip code. Walk-in appointments are also available at neighborhood locations. Advertisement The 2026-2027 School Year Immunization Requirements for NYS can be found HERE . “ Earlier is better when it comes to getting protected against illness ,” said John Marraffa, R.Ph., President of Kinney Drugs. “ Kinney is now ready to address the upcoming flu season with plenty of vaccine supply and easy, comfortable options to help our patients and communities stay healthy .” Anyone can get sick; however, research shows that some populations are at a higher risk for developing serious complications. “ Serious illness can happen to anyone, but some populations are at higher risk ,” Marraffa said. “ Older adults, people with chronic conditions like asthma, diabetes, or heart disease, those who are pregnant, and young children can all experience more severe flu outcomes. Getting vaccinated every year is important, to protect yourself and the people you care about .” You can learn more by visiting their website , downloading the new Kinney Drugs app, or speaking with their local Kinney Drugs pharmacy team. Advertisement The 2026-2027 School Year Immunization Requirements for NYS can be found HERE . “ Earlier is better when it comes to getting protected against illness ,” said John Marraffa, R.Ph., President of Kinney Drugs. “ Kinney is now ready to address the upcoming flu season with plenty of vaccine supply and easy, comfortable options to help our patients and communities stay healthy .” Anyone can get sick; however, research shows that some populations are at a higher risk for developing serious complications. “ Serious illness can happen to anyone, but some populations are at higher risk ,” Marraffa said. “ Older adults, people with chronic conditions like asthma, diabetes, or heart disease, those who are pregnant, and young children can all experience more severe flu outcomes. Getting vaccinated every year is important, to protect yourself and the people you care about .” You can learn more by visiting their website , downloading the new Kinney Drugs app, or speaking with their local Kinney Drugs pharmacy team. Symptoms often overlap, but doctors look for these clues before deciding H1N1 or seasonal flu? Symptoms often overlap, but doctors look for these clues before deciding Aadya Jha / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 17, 2026, 18:00 IST Share AA +Text Size Small Medium Large Follow us 1/7 How doctors separate flu types A fever arrives suddenly. Then come the body aches, cough, sore throat and exhaustion. For many people, the first thought is, “Is this H1N1 or seasonal flu?” The harder truth is that symptoms alone usually cannot answer that question. H1N1, more precisely influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, is itself a type of influenza. It can cause an illness that looks remarkably similar to other seasonal influenza infections. Doctors therefore do not simply look at how high the fever is or how badly the body hurts. They look at the whole picture, including how the illness is progressing, the person's health, exposure history and, when needed, testing. 2/7 Fever and body ache cannot reveal the strain “It is a major mistake to try to distinguish between H1N1 and seasonal flu by asking which causes more fever or body pains. There is no reliable checklist of symptoms that can make this distinction,” explained Dr Manisha Mendiratta, Director & Head - Pulmonology, Sarvodaya Hospital, Sector-8, Faridabad. Both can cause fever or chills, cough, sore throat, tiredness, headache, muscle aches and a blocked or runny nose. Some patients may also develop vomiting or diarrhoea. That overlap is exactly why guessing the strain at home can be misleading. Even a person with influenza may not have every classic symptom. 3/7 Doctors watch what happens after the first few days The illness trajectory can tell a doctor more than one isolated symptom. “The genuine test in flu season isn't identifying H1N1; it's spotting deterioration before it becomes a crisis,” said Dr Vijay Arora, Principal Director & Head, Department of Internal Medicine at Yashoda Medicity. He explained that many people with uncomplicated flu-like illness improve within the first few days. But a fever that continues beyond 72 hours, or disappears and then returns, deserves another medical assessment. Age and existing health problems also change the picture. An older adult, pregnant woman, or person with heart or lung disease may need closer monitoring even when the initial symptoms appear mild. 4/7 Breathing problems change the urgency There is another clue doctors take particularly seriously: how well the lungs are coping. “H1N1 has many similarities with seasonal influenza, so any kind of diagnosis is impossible without taking into account other factors apart from the symptoms,” said Dr Harish Kumar Verma, Director, Institute of Respiratory Medicine at ShardaCare - Healthcity. He highlighted breathing difficulty, chest pain, reduced oxygen levels, marked drowsiness and difficulty eating as warning signs that should not be brushed aside. This is an important distinction. The question should not only be “Which flu is this?” It should also be “Is this person getting worse?” 5/7 A test may identify influenza, but not every patient needs one Doctors can use respiratory samples to detect influenza. Depending on the test, these can include rapid antigen tests and molecular tests. More sensitive molecular testing can provide a clearer answer when identifying influenza or a particular subtype matters. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's current flu testing guidance notes that symptoms alone cannot confirm influenza. It also explains that rapid tests can be less accurate than molecular tests, meaning a negative rapid result does not always rule out flu. Testing is therefore not automatically necessary for every person with fever and cough. “Testing is important only when it impacts the choice of treatment or infection control,” Dr Mendiratta said. “Clinical judgement is more important than guessing the strain.” 6/7 The bigger clue may be the patient's changing condition Doctors also consider what is circulating in the community. If flu-like illnesses are increasing locally, that information can strengthen the clinical suspicion. But the patient's condition remains central. “Do not focus on naming the disease, but on early recognition of influenza and starting treatment while avoiding antibiotics which do not work against influenza,” Dr Mendiratta said. Antibiotics do not treat influenza because influenza is caused by a virus. Antiviral treatment may be considered by doctors, particularly for people at higher risk of complications or those who become seriously ill. So, there is no simple H1N1-versus-seasonal-flu symptom chart that can reliably settle the question. The smarter approach is to watch the illness itself. A fever that is improving is different from one that keeps returning. A cough is different from worsening breathlessness. And a mild illness in a healthy young adult is not the same situation as the same symptoms in a pregnant woman or an older person with underlying disease. The strain name matters in some situations. But recognising deterioration early can matter far more. 7/7 Medical experts consulted This article includes expert inputs shared with TOI Health by: Dr Vijay Arora, Principal Director & Head, Department of Internal Medicine at Yashoda Medicity. Dr Harish Kumar Verma, Director, Institute of Respiratory Medicine at ShardaCare - Healthcity. Dr Manisha Mendiratta, Director & Head - Pulmonology, Sarvodaya Hospital, Sector-8, Faridabad. Inputs were used to explain how doctors distinguish H1N1 from seasonal flu, why symptoms alone cannot confirm the strain, and which warning signs require timely medical attention. Testing is therefore not automatically necessary for every person with fever and cough. “Testing is important only when it impacts the choice of treatment or infection control,” Dr Mendiratta said. “Clinical judgement is more important than guessing the strain.” 6/7 The bigger clue may be the patient's changing condition Doctors also consider what is circulating in the community. If flu-like illnesses are increasing locally, that information can strengthen the clinical suspicion. But the patient's condition remains central. “Do not focus on naming the disease, but on early recognition of influenza and starting treatment while avoiding antibiotics which do not work against influenza,” Dr Mendiratta said. Antibiotics do not treat influenza because influenza is caused by a virus. Antiviral treatment may be considered by doctors, particularly for people at higher risk of complications or those who become seriously ill. So, there is no simple H1N1-versus-seasonal-flu symptom chart that can reliably settle the question. The smarter approach is to watch the illness itself. A fever that is improving is different from one that keeps returning. A cough is different from worsening breathlessness. And a mild illness in a healthy young adult is not the same situation as the same symptoms in a pregnant woman or an older person with underlying disease. The strain name matters in some situations. But recognising deterioration early can matter far more. 7/7 Medical experts consulted This article includes expert inputs shared with TOI Health by: Dr Vijay Arora, Principal Director & Head, Department of Internal Medicine at Yashoda Medicity. Dr Harish Kumar Verma, Director, Institute of Respiratory Medicine at ShardaCare - Healthcity. Dr Manisha Mendiratta, Director & Head - Pulmonology, Sarvodaya Hospital, Sector-8, Faridabad. Inputs were used to explain how doctors distinguish H1N1 from seasonal flu, why symptoms alone cannot confirm the strain, and which warning signs require timely medical attention. Drones target Kurdish leaders after Trump names them as key to US talks with IRGC Hawaii’s 1905 mosquitofish import now linked to native species decline The introduction of mosquitofish in Hawaii has dramatically affected the ecosystem, leading to notable declines in native aquatic insects. These invasive fish fiercely prey on local species, disrupting food chains. The native damselflies, unprepared for such predation, are particularly vulnerable, seeing their populations plummet. Additionally, mosquitofish compete with endemic fish and crustaceans for limited food resources, complicating control efforts due to intricate waterways and their fast breeding habits. news.content_zh: 文章讨论了印度贾坎德邦的一次抗议活动,那里有六名学生进行绝食,要求印度中央调查局对取消 JSSC-CGL 考试和涉嫌违规行为进行调查。这次抗议凸显了人们对政府处理局势的担忧,国大党领袖拉胡尔·甘地敦促首席部长亲自会见学生。贾坎德邦政府尚未采取具体行动解决抗议者的要求,该组织已宣布计划于 8 月 20 日袭击首席部长官邸。文章没有提供与抗议相关的具体病例数、死亡人数或健康影响,而是重点关注政治和行政反应。内容来源于《印度时报》,发表于2026年8月17日,为完整原创报道。
